## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. The rewrite of `requirement_proven` removes the old empty-input guard, so a requirement with no criteria is now reported as proven. `reviewed_batch` and its tests look correct.

## Critical
- app/proof.py:3 — correctness — The old code was `bool(criteria) and all(...)`. The new `return proven == len(criteria)` returns `True` for `requirement_proven([])`, because `0 == 0`. Before this change the same call returned `False`. The new test at tests/test_proof.py:6-8 never passes an empty list, so nothing catches this. Could you restore the guard, for example `return bool(criteria) and proven == len(criteria)`, or raise `ValueError` the way `reviewed_batch` does? Please also add `assert not requirement_proven([])`. — Any requirement with no criteria attached is now reported as proven even though it has no evidence.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- app/proof.py:2 — correctness — `sum(item["proven"] for item in criteria)` adds up the raw values instead of checking whether each one is truthy, which is what the old `all()` did. With `[{"proven": 2}, {"proven": 0}]` the sum is 2, which equals `len(criteria)`, so the function returns `True` even though one criterion is unproven. A string value such as `{"proven": "yes"}` raises `TypeError`. Would `all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)` behind the restored non-empty guard work for you, or `sum(bool(item["proven"]) ...)` if you want to keep the count? — Any non-boolean `proven` value either gives the wrong proof status or crashes the summary.

## Strengths
- `reviewed_batch` raises a clear `ValueError` on an empty batch. tests/test_proof.py:11-17 covers that error path, the single-entry and multi-entry all-reviewed cases, and both kinds of failing batch.
